audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere', sequencingCues = 0. Neither layer contains a single number. full.breakdown.cooldowns names Miasma but gives no cooldown and fills its other two bullets with 'Your committal tool' and 'Your ultimate' placeholders.
audit.why: This matchup has the cleanest sequencing fact in the whole slice and it was never written down. Miasma is 24/22/20/18/16s and it grounds — Riot's own text says 'Grounded enemies cannot use Movement abilities' — while Zac's Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9s. At rank 1 her grounding tool is on a LONGER cooldown than his engage, which means she can hold Miasma purely to deny the slingshot and still have it back before he does. That single comparison tells the Zac player exactly why walking up feels impossible and exactly what to wait for. Petrifying Gaze at 120/100/80s is the second number, and Noxious Blast's flat 3.5s and Twin Fang's flat 0.75s are what make her chip feel unanswerable.
audit.corrected: Added the 24s-versus-21s comparison to dontsFull[0].d, Miasma's 24s to wants.you[1], whys[2], spikes[0].text, dosFull[0].d, phases[1].why, breakdown.cooldowns and report[5].t, and Petrifying Gaze's 120s to spikes[1].text and phases[4].why.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early calls it 'Q and E poison' and 'her ramping E', content.whys[1] says 'her ramping E damage', and content.spikes[0].text says 'her E slows'. Twin Fang neither applies poison, ramps, nor slows.
audit.why: Riot's text: Twin Fang 'deals increased damage to Poisoned targets and heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt'. It consumes a poison it does not apply. The poison comes from Noxious Blast, and the slow comes from Miasma. This is the most important correction in the matchup because it inverts the counterplay: Twin Fang is not an unavoidable ramping DPS ability, it is conditional, and a Zac who is not poisoned takes a fraction of the damage and gives her no healing at all. The guide currently presents her damage as something to be endured rather than something with an off switch.
audit.corrected: Rewrote early, whys[1] and spikes[0].text so Noxious Blast applies the poison, Twin Fang feeds off it, and Miasma owns the slow and the grounding.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json Q, W and E descriptions

audit.whatIsWrong: content.mid says to beat Petrifying Gaze by approaching 'from odd angles' and content.wants.you[0] says to 'Angle your engage so her R can't catch you facing her'. The angle of approach is not what the ability checks.
audit.why: Riot's text: it stuns 'any enemies in front of her that are FACING her' and slows 'any others with their BACK TURNED'. The check is the direction the target is facing at the moment it lands, not the direction they came from. Approaching from the side while still facing her gets stunned exactly the same. The actual counterplay — turn your back as it lands and take a slow instead of a stun — is a real, executable piece of tech and the guide replaces it with something that does not work.
audit.corrected: Rewrote mid, spikes[1].text, wants.you[0], whys[4] and phases[4].why around the facing rule, and added the 120s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[10].t is the generic 'Your CC is premium gank setup — ping your jungler when Miasma is down. Ward river before extended trades.' It never mentions the thing that makes ganks decisive here.
audit.why: content.mid and content.late both note in passing that Cassiopeia has no escape, and the kit confirms it — nothing in Serpentine Grace, Noxious Blast, Miasma, Twin Fang or Petrifying Gaze is a dash or a blink. Her only mobility is a Move Speed bonus on Noxious Blast, amplified by her passive. A completely dashless enemy is the single strongest gank-priority signal a laner can give a jungler, and it is buried in a subordinate clause instead of being the headline of the jungle card.
audit.corrected: Rewrote report[10].t to lead with the no-dash fact.
sources: champ-data/_kits/cassiopeia.json full ability list, no dash flag anywhere

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t lists Heartsteel, Spirit Visage, Thornmail and Mercury's Treads and contains no Grievous Wounds source, despite _missing-interactions.json flagging needs-antiheal for this pairing.
audit.why: Twin Fang heals her for a percentage of the damage dealt, and it fires on a 0.75s cooldown against a poisoned target — so in an extended trade it is not incidental sustain, it is the reason her health bar refuses to move. The anti-heal timing is tied to the poison rather than to a level: Grievous Wounds only matters while she is landing Noxious Blast on you.
audit.corrected: Added Grievous Wounds to report[8].t and named Twin Fang as the heal.

notes: The Miasma-versus-Elastic-Slingshot cooldown comparison is the most useful thing I found in this matchup and I want to flag it beyond the audit entry: at rank 1 her grounding tool (24s) is on a longer cooldown than Zac's engage (21s), so a Cassiopeia who simply holds Miasma denies the slingshot indefinitely and still has it back first. That inverts as they rank up — by rank 5 Miasma is 16s and Elastic Slingshot is 9s — which is a genuine, checkable reason the lane gets easier for Zac with levels, and it is a better explanation for the 56.92% win rate than anything currently in either layer. Worth considering as a general pattern for the site: comparing the owner's key cooldown against the enemy's at the same rank produces sequencing advice that no stats page can generate. Deliberately not asserted: whether Petrifying Gaze can interrupt Zac's Elastic Slingshot while he is already airborne mid-flight. content.spikes[1].text currently claims 'Her R stuns you mid-air', which would be a decisive interaction if true, but cassiopeia.json needsResearch is empty and Riot's text says nothing about interrupting an in-progress dash. I removed the claim rather than repeating it, and did not replace it with a denial — it is unknown, and it deserves a wiki pass. Also note the sample here is 65 games, the smallest in the slice; the win rate is real data but thinner than the others, which is worth knowing before anyone rewrites the difficulty triple off it.
